plain.text: We who are strong ought to bear with the failings of the weak and not just please ourselves. Even Christ did not please himself. Everything written in the past was written to teach us, so that through endurance and the encouragement of the Scriptures we might have hope. May God give you a spirit of unity, so that with one mind and one voice you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

Accept one another, then, just as Christ accepted you, to bring praise to God. Christ became a servant of the Jewish people to confirm God's promises to the patriarchs, so that the Gentiles might also glorify God for his mercy. Paul quotes several Scriptures about the nations praising God. "May the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace as you trust in him, so that you may overflow with hope by the power of the Holy Spirit."

Paul is convinced the Roman believers are full of goodness and able to instruct one another, yet he has written boldly to remind them. He is a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles, offering them to God. He will only speak of what Christ has done through him to lead the Gentiles to obey God, by word and deed and the power of the Spirit. From Jerusalem all the way around to Illyricum he has fully proclaimed the gospel. His ambition has been to preach where Christ was not known.

Now there is no more place for him to work in those regions. He plans to visit Rome on his way to Spain. First he is going to Jerusalem with a gift from the churches of Macedonia and Achaia for the poor among God's people there. He asks the Romans to join him in prayer that he will be kept safe and that his service will be welcomed, so that he may come to them with joy. "The God of peace be with you all. Amen."

summary.bigIdea: Accept one another as Christ has accepted you, and overflow with hope by the power of the Spirit.
points: The strong should bear with the weak, following Christ's example.
"Accept one another, then, just as Christ accepted you."
Paul shares his mission to the Gentiles and his plans to visit Rome and Spain.
summary.reflection: Paul prays that God will fill his readers with joy, peace and hope. Which of these do you most need today?
